paper_name: Believing is Seeing Unobserved Object Detection using Generative Models

sections.abstract: This study introduces the novel tasks of 2D, 2.5D, and 3D unobserved object detection, which aim to predict the location of objects that are either occluded or located outside the camera's field-of-view. The authors adapt several state-of-the-art pre-trained generative models, including 2D and 3D diffusion models and vision-language models (VLMs), to infer the presence of these unobserved objects. To evaluate performance, a suite of metrics is proposed. Empirical evaluations on indoor scenes from the RealEstate10k and NYU Depth V2 datasets demonstrate that generative models can effectively capture spatio-semantic priors to detect objects not directly visible in an image.
sections.introduction: Object detection is typically limited to visible surfaces within a camera's field-of-view. This paper proposes going further by detecting objects that are near the camera but not observed at all, categorized into 2D, 2.5D, and 3D tasks. This is motivated by robotics tasks like visual search and navigation, where understanding the scene beyond direct observation is crucial. For instance, a robot looking for a seated person might infer the presence of additional chairs nearby. The work aims to recover spatio-semantic distributions over both observed and unobserved parts of a scene. While 3D scene generation is challenging due to occlusions and sparse data, image diffusion models and novel view synthesis offer useful priors for rendering full 3D volumes from partial observations.
sections.related work: The paper builds on several areas: 1) Object detection (e.g., YOLO, DETR) and amodal detection, which predicts the full geometry of partially occluded objects. 2) 2D diffusion models used for image outpainting and scene completion. 3) Novel View Synthesis (NVS), specifically Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and Diffusion with Forward Models (DFM), which generate 3D-consistent views from single images. 4) Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like CLIP and LLaVA, which are evaluated for their ability to perform passive inference and spatial reasoning about unobserved scene parts.
sections.unobserved object detection: The task is defined as predicting a conditional distribution $\mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{I}}$ over a bounded space and a set of semantic labels given a single RGB image $\mathcal{I}$. This spatio-semantic distribution (SSD) facilitates inferring probable locations of unobserved objects using contextual cues. The spatial domain $\mathcal{X}$ is discretized into: 1) a 2D domain $\mathbb{I}$ (a pixel grid expanding the input image) and 2) a 3D domain $\mathbb{V}$ (a voxel grid extending beyond the camera frustum). The 2D domain symmetrically extends the image width from $W$ to $W'$, while the 3D domain expands the frustum to an expanded voxel grid aligned with the camera pose.
sections.generative model-based detection pipelin: Three pipelines are detailed: 1) 3D Diffusion-based Model: Uses Diffusion with Forward Models (DFM) to generate 3D representations from a single image. It renders novel views from $k=4$ target camera poses, runs YOLOv8x on these frames, and back-projects 2D boxes into a 3D point cloud. The results are voxelized and normalized to produce the 3D distribution $\mathcal{D}_{Io}^{3D}$. 2) 2D Diffusion-based Model: Uses SDXL for outpainting to fill unobserved regions to the left and right. YOLOv8x provides confidence scores, and depth is estimated using DepthAnythingv2 to lift detections into 3D. 3) VLM-based Models: Adapts models like GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 Sonnet by querying them with binary 'Yes/No' questions regarding object presence in the original frame or extended regions. Confidence is produced from the fraction of 'Yes' responses over $n_s$ queries.
sections.experiments:
The models are evaluated on 10 indoor scenes from RealEstate10k and NYU Depth V2 using MS-COCO object categories. 

Metrics include:
- Normalized Entropy: $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{I} o} \coloneqq \frac{-1}{\log |\mathcal{X}|} \sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}} \mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{I} o}(x) \log \mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{I} o}(x)$
- Normalized Cross-Entropy: $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{I} o}^{\times} \coloneqq \frac{-1}{\log |\mathcal{X}|} \sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}} \mathcal{G}_{\mathcal{I} o}(x) \log \mathcal{D}_{\mathcal{I} o}(x)$
- Normalized Nearest Neighbor Distance: $\Delta_{\mathcal{I} o} \coloneqq \frac{1}{|\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{G}_{I o}^\tau}|} \sum_{x \in \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{G}_{I o}^\tau}} \min_{x' \in \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{D}_{I o}^\tau}} \frac{\| x - x' \|}{\text{diam}(\mathcal{X})}$
- False Negative Rate: $\text{FNR} \coloneqq \frac{\sum_{\mathcal{I} \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{o \in \mathcal{O}} y_{\mathcal{I} o} (1 - \hat{y}_{\mathcal{I} o})}{\sum_{\mathcal{I} \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{o \in \mathcal{O}} y_{\mathcal{I} o}}$
- 2D Region-wise Accuracy: $\mathcal{A}_{\mathcal{I} o} \coloneqq \frac{1}{\ell} \sum_{i=1}^{\ell} y_{\mathcal{I} o}^i \hat{y}_{\mathcal{I} o}^i + (1 - y_{\mathcal{I} o}^i)(1 - \hat{y}_{\mathcal{I} o}^i)$

Results show that for the 2D task, the 2D diffusion model (SDXL) performs best, while VLMs struggle with spatial reasoning. For 2.5D and 3D tasks, the 3D diffusion model (DFM) consistently outperforms the 2D model. Ablation studies indicate that performance decreases as the number of camera poses ($k$) or samples ($n_s$) is reduced. For SDXL, including object cues in text prompts significantly improves performance.
sections.conclusion: The paper introduces the unobserved object detection task and demonstrates that generative models can predict objects outside the visible frustum. 3D pipelines (DFM) are capable of detecting fully occluded objects, whereas 2D outpainting and VLMs are limited to out-of-frame detections. Key limitations include the high inference time of 3D diffusion models and the potential bias introduced by object prompts. Future work will explore outdoor scenes, synthetic datasets for known conditional distributions, and applications in robotics planning and navigation.
sections.supplementary:
The supplementary material provides details on: 
- Appendix A: Methodology for selecting 10 indoor scenes from RealEstate10k and NYU Depth V2. Filtering criteria included scene size (fewer than 50 images excluded), camera movement (minimum geodesic distance > 0.01), and semantic content (at least 50% of frames containing objects with confidence $\ge 0.5$). It also describes the end-to-end object selection pipeline and the parameter calibration for the threshold $\tau \coloneqq \lambda/|\mathcal{X}| > 1/|\mathcal{X}|$, with $\lambda \approx 1.4$ identified as a heuristic breaking point.
- Appendix B: 3D scene reconstruction details using SIFT for feature extraction and COLMAP/GLOMAP for pose estimation and depth map generation. 
- Appendix C: Additional implementation details, including the use of a KDTree for computing $\Delta$, DFM sampling/filtering (using Laplacian variance and SSIM to reject noisy frames), and the selection of target poses in $SE(2)$.
- Appendix D: VLM sampling methodology, detailing the binary query format and the answer retrieval pipeline used to generate confidence values.
- Appendix E: Additional results, including qualitative analysis of SDXL samples, failure case analysis (57% from prediction errors, 43% from detector false negatives), and performance on outdoor scenes (e.g., detecting 'car'). It also includes extensive ablation tables for DFM and SDXL across different configurations of samples and poses.
